## Walkthrough

This PR converts the Header class fields from mutable public properties to immutable readonly properties and refactors header construction across multiple files from mutating `Header.empty()` to using the `Header.create()` factory pattern. Changes affect the Header class definition, header construction in block-json and block modules, and header setup in two test files. No exported API signatures change except field mutability declarations. All behavioral logic remains intact.

## Estimated code review effort

🎯 3 (Moderate) | ⏱️ ~20 minutes

- **Header class field declarations**: 10 fields converted from public to readonly across a single file—repetitive but requires verification that all usages align with immutability
- **Header construction refactoring**: Four files updated to use `Header.create()` instead of mutating fields—consistent pattern but applied in different contexts (block-json, block, and two test utilities) requiring separate verification of field mappings
- **Test utility updates**: Changes in sync.test.ts and block-verifier.test.ts use the new construction pattern—verify that test scenarios remain accurate after immutability enforcement

## Possibly related PRs

- **FluffyLabs/typeberry#573**: Modifies Header class field declarations and ordering, directly related to this PR's readonly field conversion
- **FluffyLabs/typeberry#610**: Adds and uses epochMarker and ticketsMarker header fields; this PR makes those same fields readonly and refactors their construction via `Header.create()`
- **FluffyLabs/typeberry#371**: Updates BlockVerifier tests and header construction patterns; overlaps with block-verifier.test.ts changes in this PR

`135-163`: **LGTM! Header fields are now readonly.**

The addition of `readonly` modifiers to all Header fields successfully achieves the PR objective of making the Header class immutable, improving type safety and preventing accidental mutations.

---

`126-128`: **Object.assign works correctly with readonly fields in Header.create().**

The pattern is safe and verified through existing tests and multiple usages across the codebase. Readonly is only a compile-time artifact, so `Object.assign` operates without issue at runtime. The Header class differs from ValidatorKeys, TicketsMarker, and EpochMarker intentionally—those classes have private constructors accepting field parameters, while Header's private constructor takes no parameters, necessitating the `Object.assign(Header.empty(), h)` approach. The header.test.ts test suite confirms this pattern compiles and functions as intended.

</blockquote></details>
